questions.question: Georg Simon Ohm in whose honour we have the famous Ohm’s Law, hailed from which country?
questions.questionHtml: Georg Simon Ohm in whose honour we have the famous Ohm’s Law, hailed from which country?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 1: The famous physicist Georg Simon Ohm hailed from Germany.

  • Ohm was born on March 16, 1789, in Erlangen, Bavaria.
  • While teaching in Jesuits College he undertook the experiments on Newly discovered phenomenon of Electromagnetism.
  • He observed the dependence of magnetic flux on the conductor material.
  • Later in 1827, he gave a law establishing the relationship between Voltage, Electric Current and Resistance but he was severely criticized for this and was also thrown out of his job.
  • But in 1841, the importance of his study was recognised and in 1849 he was offered a position of Experimental Physics Professor at the University of Munich.
  • The unit of Resistance has been named after him as 'Ohm'.

 Ohm's Law:

It states that amount electric current through passing a conductor is directly proportional to the voltage across two ends of it. Following its the mathematical expression for Ohm's Law.

V = IR.

    • His works are ascribe to saving millions of lives through the developments of vaccines for rabies and anthrax. 
    • Pasteur was in charge for disproving the doctrine of spontaneous generation.

Additional Information

  • Alexander Fleming
    • Alexander Fleming was a Scottish physician-scientist who was recognised for discovering penicillin.​

    • Angelina Fanny Hesse  was the first to propose the use of agar as a culture media for growing and isolating bacteria.

questions.question: Who among the following was the shortest-serving Prime Minister of India?
questions.questionHtml: Who among the following was the shortest-serving Prime Minister of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Gulzarilal Nanda.

Key Points

  • Gulzarilal Nanda served as the acting Prime Minister of India twice, each time for a short period.
  • His first term was from 27th May 1964 to 9th June 1964, following the death of Jawaharlal Nehru.
  • His second term was from 11th January 1966 to 24th January 1966, following the death of Lal Bahadur Shastri.
  • Both terms combined make him the shortest-serving Prime Minister of India, with a total of 26 days in office.

Additional Information

  • Prime Minister of India
    • The Prime Minister of India is the head of government and is appointed by the President of India.
    • The Prime Minister leads the executive branch of the Government of India and is the chief advisor to the President.
    • The Prime Minister also heads the Council of Ministers and is responsible for running the government and implementing policies.
  • Acting Prime Minister
    • An Acting Prime Minister is appointed when the incumbent Prime Minister is temporarily unable to perform duties, often due to death or resignation.
    • Gulzarilal Nanda served as Acting Prime Minister twice under these circumstances.
  • Jawaharlal Nehru
    • Jawaharlal Nehru was the first Prime Minister of India, serving from 1947 until his death in 1964.
    • His death led to Gulzarilal Nanda's first term as Acting Prime Minister.
  • Lal Bahadur Shastri
    • Lal Bahadur Shastri was the second Prime Minister of India, serving from 1964 until his death in 1966.
    • His death led to Gulzarilal Nanda's second term as Acting Prime Minister.

questions.question: Who among the following social reformers of British India was known as Lokhitwadi?
questions.questionHtml: Who among the following social reformers of British India was known as Lokhitwadi?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Gopal Hari Deshmukh.Key Points

  • Gopal Hari Deshmukh (1823-1892) was a social reformer and rationalist from Maharashtra.
  • He held the post of a judge under the British raj but wrote for a weekly Prabhakar under the pen name of Lokahitawadi on social reform issues.
  • He wrote 'Shatpatre' in the Prabhakar newspaper. In 'Shatapatre' he wrote about Political, Religious, Social, Cultural topics.
  • He was against Child Marriage, the Dowry system, Polygamy.
  • He also criticized the Caste System in society.
  • He was a supporter of Girls Education.
  • He advocated a reorganization of Indian society on rational principles and modern, humanistic, secular values.
  • He attacked Hindu orthodoxy and supported social and religious equality.
  • After bearing public criticism he served lame, blind and leprosy persons. 
  • He wrote against the evils of the caste system. He said, “If religion does not sanction social reform, then change religion”.
  • He started a weekly, "Hitechhu", and also played a leading role in founding the periodicals, Gyan Prakash, Indu Prakash, and Lokahitawadi.

Additional Information

  • Jyotiba Phule​
    • Jyotirao Phule was a social reformer, activist, and writer who lived in the 19th century in Maharashtra, India.
    • He founded the Satyashodhak Samaj in 1873 with the aim of uplifting the lower castes and women through education and social reforms.
    • The Satyashodhak Samaj was a movement that challenged the caste system and advocated for social equality and justice.
    • Jyotirao Phule was also a strong advocate of women's education and established the first school for girls in Pune in 1848.
  • Veeresalingam Pantulu ​
    • Veeresalingam Pantulu (16 April 1848 – 27 May 1919) was a famous social reformer and writer of the modern period of Telugu literature.
    • He was known by the title 'Gadya Tikkana' and was often considered 'Raja Ram Mohan Roy' of Andhra.

    • He established widow ashrams and formed an association for Widow Remarriage in Madras Presidency.
    • To encourage women's education, he established schools for girls in 1874 at Dowlaiswaram near Rajahmundry.

questions.question: Which of the following Presidents of India also served as the Union Labour Minister?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following Presidents of India also served as the Union Labour Minister?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is V.V. Giri.

Key Points

  • When the Congress Party formed a government in Madras state (now Tamil Nadu) in 1937, Giri became minister of labor and industries.
  • With the resignation of the Congress governments and the launching of the anti-British “quit India” movement in 1942,
  • He returned to the labour movement and was subsequently imprisoned with his colleagues.
  • In 1952 was elected to the Lok Sabha, one of the two chambers of the Indian Parliament. He was made minister of labour in the central Indian government but resigned in 1954.
  • In 1967 he was elected vice president of India and on the death of President Zakir Husain in 1969, Giri became acting president and announced his intention to stand for the presidency.
  • He was the President of India from 24 August 1969 to 23 August 1974.

Important Points 

  • Zakir Husain, the first Muslim to hold the largely ceremonial position of president of India. 
    • he helped found the Muslim National University in Aligarh (later moved to New Delhi) and served as its vice-chancellor from 1926 to 1948.
    • In 1956–58 he served on the executive board of the United Nations Educational, Scientific, and Cultural Organization (UNESCO).
    • He was appointed governor of Bihar state in 1957 and was elected vice president of India in 1962. As the official Congress Party candidate, he was elected president of India in 1967 and served until his death.
  • Ram Nath Kovind, (born October 1, 1945, Paraukh, Uttar Pradesh state, India), Indian lawyer and politician who served as president of India (2017).
    • He was the second person from the Dalit caste, after Kocheril Raman Narayanan.
  • Neelam Sanjiva Reddy, who had been elected president in 1977, called for new elections and dissolved parliament in the winter of 1979.

Additional Information

  • Dr. Rajendra Prasad was elected as the first the President of India.
  • Ram Nath Kovind took his charge as president on July 25th, 2017, became the 14th Indian President.
  • On 21 July 2022, Draupadi Murmu has been elected as the 15th President of India.

questions.question: Who among the following became a part of the Constituent Assembly from Madras Constituency in 1946?
questions.questionHtml: Who among the following became a part of the Constituent Assembly from Madras Constituency in 1946?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Ammu Swaminathan.

Key Points

  • Ammu Swaminathan was elected to the Constituent Assembly from the Madras Constituency in 1946.
  • She spoke on fundamental rights and directive principles.
  • Ammu Swaminathan was born in 1894 in Palakkad, Kerala.
  • In 1917, she worked with Kamaladevi Chattopadhyay, Annie Besant, Muthulakshmi Reddy, and others to set up the Women’s India Association (WIA) at Adyar, Madras.
  • Swaminathan was involved in the Quit India Movement in 1942 which led to her imprisonment a year later.
  • Post-independence she was elected to the first Lok Sabha in 1952 and subsequently to the Rajya Sabha in 1954.​

Important Points

  • Kamla Chaudhry
    • Kamla Chaudhry was one of those 15 women who were a part of the Constituent Assembly.
    • She was also a talented short story writer and freedom fighter.
    • Kamla actively took part in the Civil Disobedience Movement of 1930.
    • She was jailed several times for her participation in the movement for independence.
    • During the movement, she joined Indian National Congress.
    • She was the senior Vice-Chairperson during the fifty-fourth session of the All India Congress Committee.
  • Hansa Jivraj Mehta​
    • ​Mehta was one of the 15 women framers of the Indian Constitution.
    • She was elected to the Constituent Assembly from Bombay under a Congress Party ticket.
    • In the Assembly, she strongly argued in favor of women’s rights and intervened in debates on uniform civil code and reservations.
    • Mehta participated in the non-cooperation and swadeshi movements.
    • Her involvement with India’s freedom struggle got her arrested in 1932.
  • Begum Aizaz Rasul
    • ​Rasul stepped into electoral politics in 1937 when she was elected as a member of the U.P. Legislative Assembly.
    • She continued to be a member of the U.P. Assembly until 1951.
    • Rasul was among the very few women, legislators to be elected from a non-reserved province in British India- a remarkable achievement.
    • She was a strong opponent of reservation for minorities in legislative assemblies, the partition of India, and feudal practices like the zamindari system. ​

Additional Information

  • Formation of the constituent assembly
    • ​Under the Cabinet Mission Plan of 1946, elections were held for the Constituent Assembly.
    • The members were elected by the members of the provincial assemblies by the method of a single transferable vote of proportional representation.
    • In the beginning, there were 389 members. But after the partition of the country into India and Pakistan, the number came down to 299
      • 229 were from the British Indian provinces while the remaining 70 were from the princely states.
    • The seats to the British Indian provinces and princely states were allotted in the proportion of their respective population and were to be divided among Muslims, Sikhs and the rest of the communities.

questions.question: Ranjeet Singh belonged to which Misal of the Sikh community?
questions.questionHtml: Ranjeet Singh belonged to which Misal of the Sikh community?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Sukarchakia.

Key Points

  • Ranjeet Singh, also known as Maharaja Ranjeet Singh, was the founder of the Sikh Empire in Punjab.
  • He belonged to the Sukarchakia Misal, one of the prominent Misals (confederacies) of the Sikh community during the 18th century.
  • The Sukarchakia Misal was named after its founder, Nawab Sukha Singh.
  • Ranjeet Singh successfully unified various Sikh Misals and established a powerful empire, with Lahore as its capital.

Additional Information

  • Misal
    • A Misal was a sovereign state or confederacy in the Sikh tradition, each led by a different chief or leader known as a Misaldar.
    • There were 12 prominent Misals in the 18th-century Sikh confederacy, including Sukarchakia, Ahluwalia, Kanhaiya, and Bhangi.
    • These Misals were primarily military and political organizations that played a crucial role in defending Sikh territories against external invasions.
  • Maharaja Ranjeet Singh
    • Born on 13 November 1780, Ranjeet Singh became the leader of the Sukarchakia Misal after his father's death.
    • He is credited with establishing a unified Sikh Empire in the early 19th century, encompassing parts of present-day India and Pakistan.
    • His reign marked the consolidation of the Sikh territories and the establishment of a strong and efficient administrative system.
    • Ranjeet Singh's leadership and military prowess earned him the title of "Sher-e-Punjab" (Lion of Punjab).
  • Lahore
    • Located in present-day Pakistan, Lahore served as the capital of the Sikh Empire under Maharaja Ranjeet Singh.
    • The city became a center of cultural, economic, and political activities during his reign.
    • Ranjeet Singh's administration brought about significant developments in infrastructure, including the construction of roads, canals, and forts.
  • Sikh Empire
    • The Sikh Empire was a major power in the Indian subcontinent during the early 19th century.
    • It was established by Maharaja Ranjeet Singh, who unified various Sikh Misals and expanded the empire's territory through conquests and alliances.
    • The empire's administration was known for its secular policies, promoting religious tolerance and inclusivity.
    • The Sikh Empire eventually fell to the British East India Company in the mid-19th century, following the Anglo-Sikh wars.
